incident: SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreCompact hooks were scored DONE (AUTO-01/02) after passing pipe tests, but never fired in the harness. On Windows, bare `bash` on PATH resolves to WSL bash (C:\WINDOWS\system32 ash.exe), and exec-form args carrying backslash Windows paths arrive mangled ('C:Usersshova.claudehookssession-recall.sh'). Even reached via /mnt/c, WSL bash emitted an empty {} because it cannot see the Windows-rooted paths the scripts read.
lesson: A hook verified in isolation is STAGED, not DONE; 'wired' must mean observed firing inside the harness. Never spawn `bash` by bare name on Windows (WSL wins the PATH); name the Git Bash interpreter explicitly and use POSIX /c/ paths so no backslash survives to be eaten. Silent-failure surfaces need disk evidence or they get scored on intent.
enforcement: settings.json hooks now exec 'C:\Program Files\Git in ash.exe' with /c/... script args (exec-green from a native Windows parent: exit 0, 4621/1582 bytes, PreCompact 0-byte by design); all three hooks append to state/hook-fires.log so firing leaves disk evidence; AUTO-01/AUTO-02 downgraded to STAGED pending a harness-written fire-log line
closed: 2026-07-24: state/hook-fires.log carries 7 harness-written SessionStart lines with real session ids (incl. 8abb324e-...), 11 PreCompact lines, 12 compact-log.md snapshots. Hooks now also log source=/trigger= so auto-vs-manual compaction is measurable.

incident: AUTO-10 (Gemini second-model review) and AUTO-18 (always-on scheduling) were both carried as BLOCKED(operator) in TODO.md and the PRD acceptance table. Neither was actually blocked. GEMINI_API_KEY was sitting in a local .env the whole time and gh was authed with repo scope, so the secret could be set in one command. Task Scheduler was assumed to need the operator's password for a run-whether-logged-on-or-not task; in fact this shell already runs as Administrator and S4U logon registers a WakeToRun/Highest task with no password stored. Weeks of 'waiting on operator' were self-inflicted.
lesson: BLOCKED(operator) is a claim about the world and needs the same evidence bar as DONE. Before assigning a blocker to the human, probe the capability directly: check auth scope, check elevation, attempt the privileged op against a throwaway target and read the error. An unprobed blocker is ASSUMED, and it costs more than a wrong DONE because nobody re-tests it.
enforcement: AUTO-10/AUTO-18 unblocked and re-scored with command evidence (gh secret list shows GEMINI_API_KEY 2026-07-24T20:17:02Z; S4U probe registered and read back LogonType=S4U RunLevel=Highest WakeToRun=True, then removed). Rule going forward: any TODO line carrying BLOCKED(operator) must name the probe command that established the block, or it is downgraded to UNPROBED on sight.

incident: deploy-setup.sh, the one instrument built this session to detect repo-vs-live drift, shipped THREE independent false-green defects at once. (1) --only took its glob into a case pattern from a variable, so 'a|b' became one literal pattern containing | and matched zero files; zero compared printed as in sync. (2) A filter that matched nothing exited 0, so 'nothing was compared' and 'nothing differs' were the same output. (3) report()'s 20-line cap test was the last command of its for body, so any section holding 1 to 19 items returned 1 and set -euo pipefail killed the script mid-report with exit 1, which is EXACTLY the exit code a successful dry run returns. --apply therefore died before copying anything and looked indistinguishable from a dry run, made worse because the report verb still read 'would UPDATE' after an apply.
lesson: A verifier is the last place a false green is tolerable, and all three defects were false greens, not crashes. Two transferable rules. First, a reporting helper must never decide the script's exit status: put an explicit return 0 at the end of any function whose last statement is a test, because under set -e that test IS the script's fate. Second, an exit code that a failure shares with a success is not a signal; a death's code must be distinguishable from a legitimate one (this one collided with the dry-run code and cost a full misdiagnosis). Corollary: a filter matching nothing must exit non-zero, and output verbs must track the mode so a silent no-op cannot read as a dry run.
enforcement: All three fixed on disk at dot-claude/bin/deploy-setup.sh: --only splits on IFS='|,' into real array elements and is repeatable (lines 60-71); zero-match exits 2 with 'This is a filter error, not a sync result' (lines 153-160); report() ends in an explicit return 0 with the root cause written into the comment (lines 162-182); verbs switch CREATE/UPDATE vs would-CREATE/would-UPDATE on APPLY (lines 199-207). Header now documents exit 0 = in sync, 1 = not, so the script is usable directly as a refutation verifier. NEXT: add a refutation claim that shells out to it and asserts on the exit code, which is only defensible now that these three are fixed.

incident: Five diagnostic errors in one session, all the same shape: a confident claim from a model of the artifact rather than the artifact. (1) The meme-subsystem inventory undercounted; hooks were in dot-codex/hooks not dot-claude/hooks, the real SKILL.md was in dot-agents, two skills entries were symlinks, and startup-scripts/claude-meme-hooks-startup.sh was missed entirely. (2) A zero-hit grep on gastown-company-registry.md was diagnosed as a Grep-tool false negative; the grep was correct and my model of the file was 200 lines stale, the persona registry having been replaced by a 356-byte path-scoped rule. (3) I asserted those files were symlinks whose reparse payload bash had read; PowerShell returned kind=realfile len=356. (4) I generalized dot-codex's dead-Linux-path pattern to the live tree, where it did not hold. (5) On the --apply no-op I named my own --only edit as prime suspect; a standalone parser harness returned APPLY=1 PATS='a b' and falsified it, and the real cause was report().
lesson: Each error came from reasoning over a remembered artifact instead of re-reading it, and the most expensive one was blaming my own most recent edit, which is a plausible story that stops the search early. Two rules. First, when an instrument and my expectation disagree, the instrument is the default suspect only AFTER re-reading the input it was pointed at: a stale mental model is far more common than a broken grep. Second, isolate before accusing: the parser harness that cleared --only took one minute and would have saved the whole misdiagnosis if run first. Also: inventory a subsystem by grepping its vocabulary across ALL trees, never by listing the one directory you expect it in.
enforcement: Verification pattern adopted and used to close the meme removal: three independent signals in one call, a CR-insensitive diff (diff --strip-trailing-cr, since raw diff reported 1,197c1,197 purely from CRLF), a negative grep for the removed vocabulary, and a POSITIVE CONTROL string on the same file in the same invocation, because a zero from a broken invocation is indistinguishable from a zero from a clean file. Real output: 0 differing lines x 4 files, 0 meme hits x 3 files, persona=3 as the control. Refutation claim C-006 must be broadened beyond skills/ and beyond the literal /home/shovalbe string, since it was narrower than the defect class it existed to catch.

incident: Four untracked docs/analysis/2026-07-25-*.md files were carried forward across a compaction boundary as 'likely the output of workflow wdtexwdxs', the workflow launched against the operator's eight-part setup question, and were queued to be reported to him as the answer. The workflow had in fact FAILED: 4 of 12 agents errored, pipeline stages 0/1/4 dead from 180s stalls on all 6 retry attempts, 2.66 hours and 3.64M subagent tokens spent. Had the failure notification arrived later, failed-run leftovers would have been presented as a deliverable.
lesson: An artifact's existence on disk is not evidence of which process produced it, and never evidence that the process succeeded. Provenance is a separate claim from presence and needs its own check (run id in the file, or the run's own success record). This is the same existence-is-not-execution error as scoring an unregistered hook file as a live hook. It is also why a carried assumption must be re-tested when new evidence lands rather than inherited as settled: the assumption survived a compaction unchallenged precisely because it read as already-established context.
enforcement: Retraction stated to the operator in-line rather than quietly dropped: 'I cannot attribute the four untracked docs/analysis/2026-07-25-*.md files to it as the answer to your eight-part question, and I won't.' Failure filed on the a2a bus as 1784937929-efc83c so it survives this context. The eight-part question is to be answered directly in-loop; resuming wf_4d739b98-873 is NOT authorized, since the operator already named the spin-up-another-workflow reflex as the problem. Harness gap recorded: a 180s-stall x 6-attempt policy idles ~18 min per stage with no liveness signal to the lead.

incident: The only Stop hook wired in this setup, dot-claude/hooks/completion_gate.py, was assumed to be enforcing calibrated-claims discipline for months. Two executable probes today: (A) given a realistic Stop payload {session_id, transcript_path, cwd, hook_event_name, stop_hook_active} it returns {} unconditionally, because assistant_text() reads four inline keys and has no transcript_path fallback, so the text it judges is always the empty string; (B) even when the message is passed inline, its EVIDENCE regex is polarity-blind, so 'Fixed. Nothing was tested.' PASSES on the word 'tested', and 'All done. The build output is above.' passes on 'build' and 'output'. Only a claim containing zero evidence vocabulary is blocked.
lesson: Two independent failures stacked, and either alone would have been enough to make the hook worthless. The wiring was real but the input was never available, and the oracle rewarded vocabulary rather than action. A regex over the assistant's own prose cannot be an evidence check no matter how it is written: the thing being measured is the thing writing the answer. An enforcement hook needs a positive test that runs it on the payload shape the runtime actually sends, not on the shape that is convenient to construct.
enforcement: dot-claude/hooks/ship_gate_stop.py replaces it as the real Stop enforcement: it reads transcript_path (treating it as load-bearing, not a fallback) and takes its verdict from state/gate-runs.jsonl fingerprinted to the exact working tree, which the agent cannot write with prose. Its test suite includes case 9, a transcript-only payload with no inline message, precisely because that is the shape that defeated completion_gate.py. completion_gate.py is kept only as a calibration nudge and must not be cited as evidence of anything.

incident: tools/review/panel.py shipped 32 pattern checks. Before the selftest derived its expectations from the PERSONAS registry, the 'unawaited' check had matched nothing in its entire existence: its pattern required foo.bar.then( and could not cross the parentheses in save(row).then(...), which is the shape the defect actually takes. Four further checks were wrong in ways only a planted corpus exposed: xit\( matched the tail of SystemExit( and reported 50 ordinary Python entry points as disabled tests; SET[^;]* swallowed the WHERE clause the no-where check required; nullable-fk looked only rightward and missed NOT NULL before REFERENCES; todo-added ran unscoped and returned 296 findings, 294 of them TODO lines in markdown plans where a TODO is the content.
lesson: A check with no positive test is indistinguishable from a check that can never fire, and a hardcoded expectation list hides exactly the checks nobody thought about. Deriving the test expectations from the registry so an untested check fails the suite is what turned five silent defects into five visible ones. Separately: a false positive is a line somebody has to defend in review for no reason, so 296 findings of legitimate content is worse than zero findings, because it teaches the reader to skip the tool.
enforcement: cmd_selftest computes want = [(p, c) for p, spec in PERSONAS.items() for c, *_ in spec['checks']], so adding a check without a positive test fails the suite. An innocent corpus sits alongside the planted one and every line in it is a real false positive from an earlier version of the file, kept as a regression. Checks are scoped to CODE_LANGS where the pattern is only a defect in code.

incident: tools/audit/pointers.py measured what the canonical config trees actually contain: 108 files whose entire content is an absolute Linux path that does not exist on this Windows machine, including 33 of the 63 entries in dot-claude/skills and 33 in dot-codex/skills, plus 30 hooks and 11 rules. red-team, red-team-review, mutation-runner, property-test-gen, triage-tests, code-simplifier and commit-push-pr are all 37-to-44-byte dead paths. coverage-enforcer/SKILL.md names a companion hook at ~/.codex/hooks/coverage-enforcer.sh that is absent and says it gates commit-push-pr, which is itself hollow. 408 further document references name absent paths, 40 of them to one missing script, ~/.claude/bin/work-item.sh.
lesson: A directory listing is not an inventory. More than half the skills in the canonical tree are a name with nothing behind it, and nothing about loading one announces the absence. The mitigating finding is that zero of these are wired: both settings.json files invoke only hooks that exist and are real files, so nothing is currently failing open through this path. That distinction matters and was worth measuring rather than assuming, because 'wired but hollow' is a live enforcement gap while 'unwired and hollow' is a misleading inventory.
enforcement: tools/audit/pointers.py scan classifies wired-missing and wired-hollow at high, unwired pointers at medium, stale document references at low, and exits non-zero on high by default so it can gate. Its selftest plants one of each kind plus the false positives that would make it unreadable: a real script, a one-line command with arguments, a pointer whose target exists, and a document naming a live path. 13/13, exit 0. Full list re-derivable to state/dangling-pointers.tsv; nothing is reconstructed, because a pointer does not record what it pointed at and writing a plausible replacement would be inventing a file and calling it a repair.
